The opportunity

Your Expertise Deserves to Be Recognised Beyond Your Job Title.

Many talented technology professionals have years of experience, meaningful technical contributions and valuable industry knowledge. However, their achievements are often difficult to demonstrate through publicly accessible, structured and independently verifiable evidence.

The Global Talent Visa requires more than a strong CV. Candidates need to demonstrate their expertise, contributions, recognition and potential within the digital technology sector.

First500days helps candidates understand where they stand and develop a structured approach to strengthening their professional profiles.

Hidden Achievements

Significant contributions often remain undocumented or confined to internal company projects.

Limited Industry Visibility

Technical expertise may not be reflected through public contributions, publications, communities or professional recognition.

Evidence Gaps

Achievements may exist but lack proper documentation, attribution and supporting evidence.

Our approach

We Build Profiles. Not Just Applications.

Our approach focuses on identifying genuine achievements, strengthening professional capabilities and building an evidence-backed profile over time.

Assessment Before Action

Understand your existing profile, identify strengths and evaluate gaps before deciding the next steps.

Evidence-Led Development

Build genuine technical contributions, document individual impact and strengthen professional visibility.

Personalised Guidance

Follow a roadmap based on your background, experience, professional goals and current evidence.

Who it's for

Is the Global Talent Visa Programme Right for You?

Designed for technology professionals exploring the Exceptional Talent or Exceptional Promise pathways.

Your job title, years of experience or employer alone do not establish eligibility. The relevance and quality of your evidence matter.

  • Professionals working in AI, Machine Learning, Data Science and Software Engineering.
  • Individuals with meaningful experience building or contributing to technology products.
  • Professionals who have led or significantly contributed to technical projects.
  • Technology founders and product leaders with demonstrable digital technology expertise.
  • Individuals with achievements that need better documentation and external visibility.
  • Professionals who can identify senior industry experts familiar with their contributions.

Scope & responsibilities

A Transparent Approach. Clear Responsibilities.

What We Do

  • Assess your professional profile.
  • Identify evidence gaps and development priorities.
  • Provide technical development and mentorship.
  • Guide real-world project and portfolio development.
  • Help document innovation and professional contributions.
  • Support thought leadership and external contribution strategies.
  • Organise evidence and prepare structured documentation.
  • Coordinate the handoff to a regulated immigration partner.

What We Don't Do

  • Guarantee endorsement or a visa.
  • Provide immigration or legal advice.
  • Submit endorsement applications as a regulated immigration adviser.
  • Manufacture professional achievements or technical contributions.
  • Buy, provide or write recommendation letters on behalf of referees.
  • Promise awards, publications or speaking opportunities.

Our responsibility is to help candidates develop genuine professional achievements and organise their evidence. Endorsement and visa decisions are independent decisions made by the relevant authorities.

The recommendation

Not every assessment ends in enrolment.

The assessment closes with one of three recommendations, based on what your evidence actually shows.

  • Proceed with the programmeYour background shows a relevant Digital Technology profile with gaps the programme can genuinely address.
  • Develop further firstBuild more genuine experience or contributions before investing in profile development, with a reassessment later.
  • Seek regulated immigration advice firstWhere Digital Technology route relevance is not established, we will say so and recommend not enrolling now.
Book a Profile Assessment →

How every assessment is built

Evidence first, conclusions second. If a portfolio project or recognition activity would not reflect your real work, we will not recommend it.

  • Each claim is labelled by evidence status: documented, candidate-asserted, not provided or contradictory.
  • Criteria are mapped against current official GOV.UK guidance, checked at the assessment date.
  • No success probability is given or implied.
  • Open questions for a regulated adviser are listed, not answered by us.

Assessments are preliminary professional profile-development assessments, not official eligibility decisions or immigration/legal advice. Recommendations depend on the information supplied and may change following verification.

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions.

Straight answers about what the programme is, and what it is not.

What is the UK Global Talent Visa?

The UK Global Talent Visa is an immigration route for individuals recognised as leaders or potential leaders in eligible fields. This programme focuses on the Digital Technology pathway.

What is the difference between Exceptional Talent and Exceptional Promise?

They represent different pathways within the Global Talent route. The appropriate pathway depends on the candidate's professional background, experience and supporting evidence.

Do I need to leave my current job?

No. The programme is designed to work alongside professional commitments. The expected weekly time commitment will be discussed during the assessment.

Does First500days guarantee endorsement or a visa?

No. Endorsement and visa decisions are made independently by the relevant authorities. First500days focuses on profile development, evidence organisation and preparation.

What if most of my work is confidential?

Confidential contributions can be assessed using appropriate redacted documentation, approved summaries and alternative corroborating evidence. Candidates should never disclose confidential employer information without permission.

Do you provide recommendation letters?

No. We help identify suitable professional referees and organise factual summaries of achievements. Recommendation letters must be independently written and approved by the referees themselves.

Do you provide immigration advice?

No. Immigration and legal advice is handled by an appropriately regulated immigration professional.

Can someone from a non-technical background apply?

The Digital Technology route has specific field and professional requirements. A profile assessment helps determine whether the candidate's experience is relevant. A different professional background does not automatically establish route suitability.

How much does the programme cost and how long does it take?

The programme structure, commercial terms and expected timeline are discussed following the initial profile assessment.
